The statement communicates a rules-consistent, credibility-focused tightening. By lifting the federal funds target to 4.25–4.50%, raising interest on reserve balances (IORB) to 4.4%, setting ON RRP at 4.3%, and continuing balance-sheet runoff, the FOMC’s stance aligns with benchmark policy rules when inflation is well above target (Federal Reserve implements Taylor-rule style policy; Fed sets the federal funds rate; introduces/pays interest on reserves). The explicit emphasis on policy lags and cumulative tightening is consistent with evidence from Romer and Romer’s narrative identification that monetary policy shocks transmit to activity and inflation with delays, warranting a cautious path of ongoing increases. Forward guidance plus QT should work through longer-term yields and term premia, in line with Cochrane–Piazzesi insights on the term structure channel. The inflation diagnosis—pandemic supply/demand imbalances and the Ukraine war—matches research on COVID-19 supply-chain shocks and geopolitical headwinds weighing on global activity. Framing the action within the 2% objective and the average-inflation approach highlighted by Chair Powell at Jackson Hole enhances policy credibility in the Volcker tradition, which can help anchor expectations and reduce the long-run cost of disinflation. Overall tone: hawkish and near-term growth-negative, but academically grounded and credibility-supportive.
